module.favicon_hash.checks: Computes the favicon fingerprint (MurmurHash3, MD5, SHA-256) and the matching search queries for Shodan, FOFA and Censys.
module.favicon_hash.fix:
Read the fingerprint and the queries offered by the module (Shodan `http.favicon.hash:FINGERPRINT`, FOFA `icon_hash="FINGERPRINT"`, Censys with the MD5): anyone can run them to find the servers that serve the same icon. Run them yourself to see what a third party sees.
Compare every result with your inventory (servers, environments, CDN, providers): every address found must be known, intended and up to date. Note the unknown addresses.
Origin server found behind a CDN: accept inbound connections only from the CDN's address ranges (firewall, security group), or use an outbound connection (tunnel) or mutual authentication of the origin, so that the CDN can no longer be bypassed by visiting the address directly.
Forgotten or unexpected instance (staging, old version, test copy, another server's panel): shut it down and delete it, or put it behind a VPN or authentication. While at it, check the DNS records that still point to it.
Default icon of a piece of software (administration panel, router, monitoring tool): it reveals the product. Restrict access to that product to your internal network and keep it up to date; replacing the icon is only a complement.
Monitor over time: set up an alert (for example Shodan Monitor or Censys on your address ranges) and repeat the search after any change of hosting, CDN or software.
After fixing, repeat the same search: the origin's direct address must no longer answer or appear in the results.
module.favicon_hash.title: Favicon fingerprint
module.favicon_hash.why: The same favicon shows up on other servers: the fingerprint helps find the origin of a site behind a CDN or other instances of the same software.
